 Bilaspur in Special Sessions Trial No. 33/2021, whereby the appellant  has been convicted under Section 363, 366 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,

 Vasim Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer, appearing for the State/respondent Amit Alias Sonu Yadav vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111242125/
1 on the instant application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (I.A. No. 1/2023).

sentences.text: Mother of the prosecutrix appeared in person and objected the application for suspension of sentence.
Learned counsel for the convict/appellant has argued that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.

It has argued that as per prosecution case, the victim was stated to be a minor girl aged about 17 years 2 months on the date of incident, which is on the basis of birth certificate, which was issued by the Choice Centre of Bilaspur (CG), but as per para 7 of statement of mother (P.W. 2) of the prosecutrix, the prosecutrix was born in State of Bihar.
It is submitted that it is a case of elopement, not the case of abducting or enticing.
The prosecutrix herself has stated in para 8 that she and appellant wanted to marry each other.
It is also submitted that since mother of the prosecutrix was against their relationship, therefore she lodged FIR.
It is further argued that appellant was on bail during trial and has not misused the liberty granted to him and the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more in its final disposal.
Hence he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the court below.

Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for both the parties, also considering the age of the prosecutrix which is 17 years and 2 months, that too, on the basis of birth certificate issued by the Choice Centre of Bilaspur (CG), whereas, as per her mother, she was born in the State of Bihar, further considering the statement of prosecutrix in which she has stated that she and appellant liked each other and they wanted to marry each other, further considering that the appellant was on bail during trial and has not misused his liberty, and hearing of this appeal would take prolonged period of time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to appellant by the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.
He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond with surety to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 22-11- 2023.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, IA No. 1/2023 is allowed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only confined for disposal of aforesaid IA filed in this appeal and it shall not be construed as an expression of opinion of this Court on the merits of the matter.
List this matter for final hearing.
